h.select_rule: Rank by: plausible mechanism supported by known empirical regularities (saturation, redundancy, optimization difficulty, capacity trade-offs) AND a direction most practitioners would not predict. Drop hypotheses that merely restate that removing a path increases the importance of the remaining ones.
h.strategy: Use the gap list to find interactions the literature leaves unsettled. Prefer conditional effects driven by diminishing returns: an edit's benefit shrinks when the parent already has that capability elsewhere, and a removal costs little when redundant capacity exists. Also consider optimization effects: extra parameters or depth can hurt in some contexts, while simple identity-like options can help trainability. Avoid hypotheses whose condition simply disconnects or trivializes the edited component. Spread hypotheses across different edited fields, conditions and both directions.

hyps.why: A direct 3x3 conv is partly redundant when the 0->1->3 two-hop path already holds a 3x3 conv, so diminishing returns shrink the gain.
The capacity a direct 1x1 conv adds is already supplied by a conv on the 0->2->3 path.
A deeper conv-heavy two-hop path benefits more from an identity shortcut that eases gradient flow.
Upgrading from 1x1 to 3x3 gives a smaller gain than upgrading from skip or pool, since a conv is already present.
Replacing an identity with a 3x3 conv adds the most new spatial capacity, so the gain exceeds that from replacing a 1x1 conv.
Pool has no learnable weights, so replacing it with a 3x3 conv gains more than replacing a conv.
A conv upstream on the same serial path already gives enough receptive field and depth, so a second conv adds less and may hurt optimization.
Downstream identity after an upstream conv keeps the path shallow and trainable.
A pool on a sibling branch where conv capacity is already present adds only smoothing, so the gain is smaller than when the sibling is weak.
Upgrading the direct edge from 1x1 to 3x3 yields a smaller gain than upgrading from skip or none, since a conv already exists.
